rationale: CoMD is a DOE molecular-dynamics proxy app: dense numeric kernels (force computation, neighbor lists, integration) with tight hot loops and no source-level metadata available, so pass selection must be conservative about loop-body overhead. SUB gets the highest security weight because arithmetic substitution obfuscates the algebraic core of force/energy computations with minimal per-iteration cost and near-zero correctness risk. SPLIT and IGV are favored for diversity at low runtime cost, since splitting and inter-group transformations frustrate static structural recovery without perturbing hot-loop inner computations. BCF and FLA carry the highest RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights because bogus control flow and control-flow flattening directly tax branch predictors and I-cache behavior in the very loops that dominate CoMD execution time, and FLA additionally carries non-trivial correctness risk around loop-carried dependencies and OpenMP-style parallel regions. IBR and ICALL sit in the middle: indirect branching/calling raises reverse-engineering resistance for the command-dispatch and lattice-setup code paths but adds indirect-branch misprediction cost, so they are weighted to apply selectively rather than uniformly. Overall the table biases toward data-oriented, low-overhead passes while gating the control-flow-heavy passes behind higher cost awareness.
